title: Talent Pathway Launchpad and Benefits Catalog
author: Priya Nandagopal
content:
Overview:

This playbook combines two companion needs for new and existing Redwood teammates: (1) a concise, repeatable career-path launchpad that clarifies role-level expectations, promotion signals, mentorship offerings, and leveling checkpoints; and (2) a compact benefits and tools catalog that new hires can use to become operational in their first 30 days. This document is intended for hiring managers, new hires, mentors, and People Ops partners.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (Priya Nandagopal)
- Promotion requests & calibration: People Ops + Engineering Managers + Product managers for PM/Design roles
- Tools & access issues: IT Services (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Benefits enrollment questions: Total Rewards (owner: Evelyn Chen)

Section 1 — Quick career-path launchpad:
1) Role families and common prefixes:
   - IC (Individual Contributor): IC1, IC2, IC3, IC4, IC5 (senior, staff, principal equivalents)
   - EM (Engineering Manager): EM1, EM2, EM3 (manager, senior manager, director equivalence)
   - PM/DES (Product/Design): PM1..PM4, DES1..DES4

2) Promotion signals (evidence we expect):
   - Impact: measurable product or infra outcomes tied to business metrics or SLOs (examples: 20% reduction in inference cost for a service; +15% query throughput)
   - Scope: cross-team influence (roadmaps, rollout ownership) and mentoring of 2+ peers for mid-to-senior levels
   - Craft: consistent delivery quality, code review leadership, and design artifacts that are followed in production
   - Leadership: for senior IC/EM bands, pattern of mentoring, hiring contributions, and representation in roadmap tradeoffs

3) Example leveling rubric highlights (short):
   - IC2 -> IC3: takes end-to-end feature ownership for a small service; consistently hits deadlines; mentors interns
   - IC3 -> IC4: owns cross-team features, leads design reviews, drives postmortem action items to closure
   - IC4 -> IC5: shapes product/architecture strategy, routinely mentors external teams, and defines technical hiring bar

4) Promotion process (7-step checklist):
   1. Candidate prepares a 1–2 page promotion packet (owner drafts evidence and impact statements)
   2. Manager reviews and adds calibration notes
   3. People Ops schedules a cross-functional calibration panel within 10 business days
   4. Panel provides decision and written feedback (target: 5 business days)
   5. Manager meets with candidate to communicate outcome and growth plan
   6. If promoted, update title and payroll change within next payroll cycle (People Ops)
   7. If delayed or appealed, escalations go to Director of People Ops (Rosa Alvarez)

Section 2 — 30/60/90 onboarding and tooling checklist (target: fully operational in 7 business days):
A) Preboarding (before Day 1):
   - IT creates account & issues laptop request (Jira ticket template: IT-NEW-HIRE)
   - People Ops sends welcome packet and benefits summary with enrollment deadlines
   - Manager assigns a buddy and schedules first-week 1:1s

B) Day 0–7 (Week 1):
   - Complete HR forms, tax, and payroll (Total Rewards link included in welcome email)
   - Access: Slack, Okta, GitHub team invites, Google Workspace, Confluence, internal AWS/GCP project access
   - Tools checklist (CLI examples):
     - Install dev image: curl -fsSL https://internal-assets.redwood.ai/devbox.sh | bash
     - Authenticate: eval $(okta-aws login --profile redwood-dev)
     - Clone standard repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-service.git
   - First-week deliverable: small bugfix or onboarding doc contribution (owner: manager)

C) Day 8–30 (Ramp):
   - Complete at least one cross-team code review and one feature PR
   - Meet with product/security/infra leads for context-richer sessions
   - Benefits enrollment deadline: 30 days from start date (see Section 3)

Section 3 — Benefits snapshot and key deadlines:
- Health: medical, dental, vision plans; enrollment window: first 30 days or Open Enrollment (owner: Total Rewards)
content_continued:
- 401(k): automatic enrollment at 3% after 60 days; company match details in Total Rewards doc
- PTO: flexible vacation policy with recommended minimum 15 business days off per year; manager must approve planned leaves in Lattice at least 2 weeks prior for >5 business days
- Parental leave: primary caregiver up to 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver up to 8 weeks paid; see parental-leave-policy for paperwork
- Sabbatical and returnship: eligibility after 4 years service; request process handled by People Ops
- Stipends: home office stipend (one-time), conference stipend (annual), learning budget per employee (owner: People Ops)

Section 4 — Mentorship, career coaching and manager responsibilities:
- Mentorship programs: 6-month matched mentorship cohorts run quarterly (owner: People Ops). Mentors and mentees sign a 3-item goal charter in Confluence.
- Manager checklist for promotion-readiness conversations: quarterly calibration, clear written feedback, and a documented growth plan with specific milestones and owners.
- Coaching: Career coaching sessions available for all mid-senior levels (request via People Ops internal form).

Section 5 — Internal tools & quick references (common commands and tickets):
- Request new service quota: open ticket in Jira under GOV-QUOTA with details: anticipated QPS, memory/GPU requirements, and expected spike windows
- Request private deployment access: fill out the Private Deployment NDA + customer onboarding template (link in Confluence)
- Observability onboarding: add service to Datadog dashboard (dashboard template: REDWOOD_INFERENCE_SERVICE_TEMPLATE). For tracing, enable X-Ray headers and register service in service-registry (CLI: rwctl register --service <name>)

Section 6 — Examples and templates (where to find them):
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/promotion-packet-template
- 30/60/90 plan template: /confluence/company-handbook/01_working-at-redwood/30-60-90-template
- GitHub PR & code review checklist: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs/pr-checklist

Appendix — Escalations and SLAs:
- Time-to-provision access SLA: 3 business days for standard requests, 7 business days for private-deployment or elevated cloud roles
- Benefits enrollment support SLA: 2 business days response from Total Rewards team on submitted cases

Contact matrix (who to ping):

- IT & Laptop/Access: it-support@redwood.ai (Jira: IT-NEW-HIRE)
- Total Rewards & benefits: benefits@redwood.ai
